provenance.benchmark_boundary: This is a rediscovery benchmark, not an observation claim. Public rows are computed from the declared generative model below at exact rational precision; they are not raw measurements, and no observational dataset is opened at run time. Published values are used only as anchors for the construction, and the residual between the constructed rows and the published values is reported under 'fidelity'.

declared_constants.perihelion_advance_coefficient_formula: 3888000*G*M/(c^2*au); the 6*pi radian-per-revolution factor times the 648000/pi arcseconds-per-radian factor leaves 3888000 with no pi remaining

fidelity.note: The semi-major-axis deviation is pure quantization. The period deviation is the physical residual of the two-body point-mass idealization against published sidereal periods (planet-mass and epoch-convention effects); it is reported, not hidden.

generative_model.world_01: x1 = s^2, x2 = s^3, where s is the published semi-major axis square root rounded to 12 decimal places
generative_model.world_02: x1 = s^2, x2 = four_pi_squared*x1/(s^3)^2, computed from the world_01 columns
generative_model.world_03: x1 = s^2, x2 = published eccentricity, x3 = advance_coefficient/(x1*(1 - x2^2))

targets.attribution: Johannes Kepler, Harmonices Mundi (Linz, 1619), Liber V, Caput III - the harmonic (third) law: the square of a planet's orbital period is proportional to the cube of its semi-major axis.

column_meanings.x1: orbital semi-major axis a, in astronomical units
column_meanings.x2: sidereal orbital period T, in Julian years

targets.statement: T = a^(3/2); equivalently T^2/a^3 = 1 in units of years and astronomical units

targets.attribution: Isaac Newton, Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica (London, 1687), Book I Propositions 1-4 and Book III Propositions 1-8 - the inverse-square law of universal gravitation: the centripetal acceleration of an orbiting body falls off as 1/r^2.

column_meanings.x1: orbital radius r, in astronomical units

targets.attribution: Albert Einstein, 'Erklaerung der Perihelbewegung des Merkur aus der allgemeinen Relativitaetstheorie', Sitzungsberichte der Koeniglich Preussischen Akademie der Wissenschaften (Berlin), 18 November 1915, pp. 831-839 - the anomalous perihelion advance per revolution, 6*pi*G*M/(c^2*a*(1-e^2)).

column_meanings.x1: orbital semi-major axis a, in astronomical units
column_meanings.x3: anomalous perihelion advance per revolution, in arcseconds

parameters.required_derived_variable: a*(1 - e^2), the semi-latus rectum in units of a

targets.statement: dphi = 6*pi*G*M/(c^2*a*(1-e^2)) per revolution; equivalently dphi*a*(1-e^2) is constant across bodies

targets.attribution: Isaac Newton, Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica (London, 1687) - the same inverse-square law as world_02.
